answer: An agent market requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can submit offers, whether the job is to audit a cipher, map a dune, or track a plume. A thousand fake bidders therefore tie up $100,000 for a month. Creating new keys does not bypass the bond: every identity needs its own deposit. The defense makes a sybil swarm consume capital and forgo interest, even if the attacker later recovers every bond.
